en.note: Individual timed project for Advanced Business Analytics at NYU, October 2026, on a course case about a fictional regional bank, shared with the instructor's permission. The segment table, the score check, the correlations and the hand-scored prospects are recomputed at build time from the two case files below; the model metrics come from the SAS Visual Analytics run submitted with the report.

fig1.title: Two models, one number per letter
fig1.caption: Exhibit 1. The bank already had a response score. The missing half was a funding model that predicts how much an account holds if it opens; Finance's rule turns the pair into the expected value of one letter, and the mail file is the top 8,000 by that value.

fig2.title: The response score ranks well and is honest about its odds
fig2.sub: 30,000 past prospects in ten equal groups by p_open · bars: actual open rate · dots: average p_open
fig2.caption: Exhibit 2. The top tenth opens at 23.5%, 3.26 times the 7.20% average, and the rate falls almost steadily to 0.97% in the bottom tenth. In every decile the average score sits within about 0.8 points of what actually happened, so the probabilities can go straight into the value formula without recalibration.

fig3.title: What predicts opening is not what predicts money
fig3.sub: Pearson correlation · left: with opening, all 30,000 prospects · right: with the funded balance, 2,161 openers
fig3.caption: Exhibit 3. Younger, digitally active prospects are the ones who open; older, higher-income prospects are the ones who fund. Age and digital engagement flip sign between the two columns. Net-worth band, the strongest driver of balance in the model, is categorical and does not appear here.

fig4.title: The segments that open most hold the least
fig4.sub: nine segments of last year's file · x: open rate · y: average 90-day balance of openers (log scale) · circle area: prospects in the new file · filled: mailed under Plan A
fig4.caption: Exhibit 4. Young prospects with under $50K net worth open at 11.8%, the highest rate, but fund $1,958 on average, just under the $2,000 line where an account stops paying for its $100 bonus. Prospects aged 45+ with $1M+ open at 3.5% and fund $37,871: worth $30.40 per letter against −$1.13.

fig5.title: Same budget, about seven times the profit
fig5.sub: 8,000 letters allocated by segment · bar length: letters · label: expected profit
fig5.planA: Plan A · highest value per letter first
fig5.planB: Plan B · highest open rate first (last year)
fig5.caption: Exhibit 5. Plan B spends 5,089 of its 8,000 letters on the young, low-net-worth segment and loses about $5,750 there. Plan A mails older and wealthier segments first and expects $119,731 against $16,825. It opens fewer accounts, which the marketing team should expect and explain.

fig6.title: Three prospects, scored by hand
fig6.sub: linear funding model applied coefficient by coefficient · negative predictions floored at $0
fig6.caption: Exhibit 6. Prospect A is 29 times as likely to open as C, but the model predicts a negative balance for A (the linear terms simply add up past zero), so every opening loses money. C rarely opens and is worth the most per letter. Mail C, then B; do not mail A.

zh.note: 纽约大学「高级商业分析」课程的个人限时项目，2026 年 10 月，案例为一家虚构的区域银行，经授课老师同意公开。分群表、评分校验、相关系数和手工评分均在构建时由下方两份案例数据重新计算；模型指标来自随报告提交的 SAS Visual Analytics 运行结果。

stats.label: 方案 A · 按价值排序
方案 B · 按响应排序

fig1.title: 两个模型，合成每封信的期望价值
fig1.caption: 图 1. 银行已有响应模型的评分，缺的是入金模型：如果客户开户，90 天内会存入多少钱。按财务部给出的公式，把两者合成一封信的期望价值，再按期望价值取前 8,000 名寄信。

nodes.name: 响应评分 p_open
nodes.num: 已提供 · 最高十分位提升度 3.26

nodes.name: 入金模型：开户后 90 天余额
nodes.num: 线性回归 · 2,161 个开户样本

fig2.title: 响应评分排序有效，概率也基本准确
fig2.sub: 30,000 名历史客户按 p_open 等分为十组 · 柱：实际开户率 · 点：平均 p_open
fig2.caption: 图 2. 评分最高的一组开户率 23.5%，是整体 7.20% 的 3.26 倍；开户率逐组下降，最低一组为 0.97%。每一组的平均评分与实际开户率相差都在约 0.8 个百分点以内，因此可以直接代入期望价值公式，无需重新校准。

fig3.title: 影响开户的因素，与影响入金的因素方向相反
fig3.sub: Pearson 相关系数 · 左：与是否开户，全部 30,000 人 · 右：与入金金额，2,161 名开户客户
fig3.caption: 图 3. 更容易开户的是年轻、数字化活跃的客户；存钱更多的是年龄较大、收入较高的客户。年龄和数字化活跃度在两列中的方向正好相反。模型中影响余额最大的净资产区间是分类变量，相关矩阵里看不到。

fig4.title: 开户率最高的群体，存的钱最少
fig4.sub: 去年数据的九个分群 · 横轴：开户率 · 纵轴：开户客户的平均 90 天余额（对数刻度）· 圆面积：新名单中的人数 · 实心：方案 A 寄信
fig4.caption: 图 4. 45 岁以下、净资产低于 5 万美元的客户开户率最高（11.8%），但平均只存入 $1,958，低于 $2,000 的盈亏线，抵不过 $100 的开户奖励。45 岁及以上、净资产 100 万美元以上的客户开户率只有 3.5%，平均存入 $37,871：每封信的期望价值为 +$30.40，前者为 −$1.13。

fig5.title: 预算相同，利润约为去年做法的七倍
fig5.sub: 8,000 封信在各分群的分配 · 条长：寄信数 · 标注：预期利润
fig5.planA: 方案 A · 按每封信的价值从高到低
fig5.planB: 方案 B · 按开户率从高到低（去年做法）
fig5.caption: 图 5. 方案 B 把 8,000 封信中的 5,089 封寄给年轻、低净资产的客户，这部分预计亏损约 $5,750。方案 A 优先寄给年龄较大、净资产较高的分群，预期利润 $119,731，方案 B 为 $16,825。方案 A 的开户数会更少，需要提前向业务方说明。

fig6.title: 手工为三位客户评分
fig6.sub: 按线性入金模型逐项系数相加 · 负的预测值按 $0 计
fig6.caption: 图 6. 客户 A 的开户概率是 C 的 29 倍，但模型给 A 的预测余额为负（线性模型只是把各项相加，会加到零以下），开户越多亏得越多。C 很少开户，但每封信的价值最高。应先寄给 C，再寄给 B，不寄给 A。
